subject.title: Agent loop allows simulated tool calls instead of enforcing real tool invocation

question: Should internal OpenClaw agent turns add a strict tool-call enforcement policy for clear tool-required requests, and should that policy be default behavior or opt-in per agent/model?
rationale: The source shows the current boundary is intentionally mixed: warning-only for unstructured tool-looking text, compatibility promotion for some standalone formats, and Gateway-only HTTP `tool_choice` enforcement. Tightening it changes both the security boundary and local-model compatibility contract.

options.title: Design opt-in strict enforcement
options.body: Add a bounded strict mode or policy contract that retries/fails closed only when the turn is explicitly tool-required, while preserving current compatibility behavior by default until maintainers approve a default change.

options.title: Make strict behavior the default
options.body: Treat clear tool-required text-only turns as failures across internal agent runs, accepting the upgrade and local-model compatibility risk as a security default change.

options.title: Fold into broader response gates
options.body: Defer this item to the larger response-gate and ledger-verification direction tracked by related issues, trading a cleaner policy model for a larger design effort.

recommendation.title: Design opt-in strict enforcement
recommendation.body: Add a bounded strict mode or policy contract that retries/fails closed only when the turn is explicitly tool-required, while preserving current compatibility behavior by default until maintainers approve a default change.

likelyOwner.reason: The core dispatch boundary and recent agent-core tool-call handling history make this the best available owner for the security/default decision.
